*Per-turn timeout** | How long one model turn (prompt → response) may run. |\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:451:An empty fi
eld shows the platform default it inherits rather than a blank — \"no value\" means \"whatever the platform decides\". Clearing a
field saves as `null`, which resets to the platform default. The API accepts these at `settings.executionBudgets.*` on the suite P
ATCH.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:453:Platform-enforced ceilings apply: a value above the platform ceiling is refused at
save time, naming the field and the bound. Organization-level ceilings are enforced by the server.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/e
vals.md:457:Each eval suite has a **Default Execution Config** section that controls the model, system prompt, temperature, tool a
pproval, connection settings, capabilities, and host context used when running the suite.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:45
9:* **Model and prompt** — Set the default model ID, system prompt, and temperature for all runs in the suite. When running evals
against MCP Apps that render widgets, the eval harness automatically enables browser interaction (screenshot, click, type) for any
model that supports both vision and tool calling — not just Claude. Models that lack vision or tool calling run without browser i
nteraction.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:478:The suite-level **system prompt** and **temperature** are runtime defaults:
when a test case does not set its own system prompt or temperature, the suite values are used for that iteration. A per-case overr
ide always wins — the suite default only fills the gap.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:482:> If you have existing suites wh
ere test cases do not specify a system prompt, those cases will now run with the suite's system prompt applied. Cases that already
set their own system prompt are unaffected.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:486:The **CI** tab (when enabled for your proje
ct) shows only CI-active suites — suites created by the SDK or suites that CI has reported into at least once. Playground-only sui
tes stay in the **Evaluate** tab. If a project has no CI evals yet, the CI tab shows a quickstart prompt.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/
docs/evals.md:557:* **Run insights** — an AI-written diff against your previous completed run: which cases moved, which tools chan
ged behavior, which models diverged. Skim this first; it usually points at the right rabbit hole. The model pass is **included wit
h MCPJam and consumes no credits**; it counts against a daily insight quota shared with swarm wave and user-testing insights. Gues
ts browsing without a signed-in account will see a **Sign in** prompt in the insights band — signing in unlocks the feature withou
t losing your place.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:558:* **Overview tab** — every run with its summary metrics, plus a Sui
te Health chart whose bars link to individual run rows. Click in for the iteration-level breakdown. The table shows **Date** first
, then **Run**, with separate **Client**, **Model**, **Platform**, **Commit**, **Rate**, **Latency**, **Tokens**, and **Calls** co
lumns. The Client column counts unique clients; when there are more than two, a **+N** badge appears — hover it to see all clients
in a tooltip.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:578:* **Stamped.** The platform decides a run's `source` itself, and a caller
cannot\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:588:strength of it. Alongside both, the platform records the credential the request\
n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:595:When two or more host configurations are attached to a suite, a **By case / By host** to
ggle appears. **By host** shows a matrix — one column per host, one row per case. Each cell shows pass/fail dots, pass rate, media
n latency, and token usage. A host detached after runs were recorded stays visible, labelled **historical**.\n/workspace/mcpjam-ev

### Payment history

The **Payment history** card on the org billing page list

s your recent credit top-ups. Each row shows:

| Column | Details |
| - | - |
| Date | When the top-up was processed |
| Amou
nt | Amount charged in USD |\n| Status | `Succeeded`, `Pending`, or `Failed` |\n| Receipt | Link to the Stripe-hosted receipt (ope
ns in a new tab) |\n\nIf a receipt isn't available yet the cell shows **Processing** (for pending charges) or **Not available** (f
or succeeded charges without a receipt link).\n\nTo add credits, click **Top up** — either from the empty state when you have no h

istory, or from the credit balance card above.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Free plan organizations cannot purchase credits directly.** If
your organization is on the Free plan, the Top up dialog shows a message that only an organization owner can upgrade the plan, wi
th a **Compare plans** button. Clicking it closes the dialog and opens your organization's Plans settings so you can upgrade.\n\n>
[!NOTE]\n>\n> **Desktop app:** When you confirm a top-up in the desktop app, checkout opens in your default system browser and th
e dialog closes automatically. Your credit balance updates in the app once the purchase completes — no redirect back into the app

is required.

### Spend budget

### Pre-run credit estimate

When enabled on your account, an **ⓘ** icon appears beside run
controls before you launch. Hovering it shows an estimated credit cost for the run about to start — priced against the exact model

s, cases, and iteration count the button will execute.

The estimate appears on:

* **Run all** in the suite header — prices e
very case × model × iterations × run plans.\n* **Per-case Run** buttons in the cases list and case sidebar — prices that case's co
